units.title: 1. GTCS Causes: Metabolic, Encephalopathy and Encephalitis
units.guide:
GTCS causes start with metabolic hypoglycemia and electrolytes, encephalopathy hepatic uremic, and encephalitis viral HSV-1 with B/L temporal hyperintensity.
Note K+ and PO4 abnormalities don't produce seizures; autoimmune anti NMDA and paraneoplastic are listed under encephalitis.

units.title: 2. Brain Injury, Post Stroke, Drugs, Withdrawal and Syncope Types
units.sec: GTCS Causes - Brain Injury, Drugs, Withdrawal and Syncope Types
units.guide:
Brain injury remote/long standing and post stroke seizures are GTCS causes, along with drug non adherence and specific epileptogenic drugs.
Withdrawal seizures include alcohol, barbiturate, benzodiazepine; syncope types are vasovagal, cardiac, orthostatic hypotension and situational.

units.title: 3. Seizure vs Syncope Table
units.guide:
Seizure vs syncope table contrasts precipitating factors, premonitory symptoms, posture, transition, duration, facial appearance and post-event features.
Seizure has usually none precipitants, aura odd odor, variable posture, immediate transition, minutes unconsciousness, 30-60 s tonic-clonic, cyanosis frothing, prolonged disorientation, muscle aching, occasional tongue bite/incontinence/headache.

units.title: 4. Management Flowchart and Antiepileptic Drugs
units.sec: Management of GTCS Flowchart and AED Choices
units.guide:
New onset seizure splits into focal LOC+ complex partial and LOC- simple partial, and generalized non motor absence and motor GTCS atonic myotonic.
AED: CPS medial temporal carbamazepine oxcarbazepine lamotrigine levetiracetam; Absence typical atypical and JME valproate lamotrigine topiramate with ethosuximide note typical <3 years; GTCS valproate > lamotrigine.

units.title: 5. Pregnancy and AED Side Effects
units.sec: Pregnancy and Side Effects of AED
units.guide:
Pregnancy best is lamotrigine least teratogenic, if already on AED folic acid supplementation.
Side effects: carbamazepine SJS, oxcarbazepine SIADH hyponatremia more than carbamazepine, lamotrigine SJS HLH/MAS, levetiracetam suicidal ideation, valproate alopecia liver NH3 pancreatitis thrombocytopenia weight gain, topiramate renal stones weight loss, zonisamide cognitive slowing, felbamate aplastic anemia, lacosamide PR prolongation.

units.title: 6. Status Epilepticus Definition, Time Points and Classification
units.guide:
Definition continuous ≥5 minutes or ≥2 discrete seizures without regaining consciousness.
Time T1 5 mins most ideal to start Rx, treatment started here normally, T2 30 mins beyond risk brain damage, 1 hr within seizure must be controlled. NORSE viral unless proven otherwise. Classification convulsive CSE, non-convulsive NCSE also post CSE, refractory unresponsive to AED + BZD.

units.title: 7. Clinical Features and EEG Monitoring
units.sec: C/F and Management - Compensatory Phase and EEG
units.guide:
Initial compensatory sympathetic overdrive ↑CO ↑BP ↑blood sugar ↑lactate.
Decompensation cardiac arrest, rhabdomyolysis + ATN + electrolyte ↓Ca ↓PO4 ↑K, MODS, ↑ICP herniation coning, hyperthermia. Mx EEG continuous monitoring ≥48h in comatose to evaluate NCSE.

units.title: 8. Status Epilepticus Management
units.guide:
Rapid IV access minimum 2 lines; No IV IM midazolam 0.2 mg/kg max10 or buccal/intranasal 0.5 mg/kg max10.
If not stop in 5 min achieve IV access; Yes IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg max4 or slow IV diazepam 1mL in 4mL NS.
Repeat lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg; shift to 2nd line through 2nd IV line valproate 30-40 @6, phenytoin 20 @50, fosphenytoin 20 @150, levetiracetam 30-40.
If not stop in 20 min 3rd line propofol phenobarbitone thiopentone.

units.title: 9. Childhood Seizures and Lafora Disease
units.guide:
Childhood seizures split into epileptic encephalopathies Lennox Gastaut West Dravet, Lafora's disease, Rolandic benign centrotemporal epilepsy.
Table West age -, Dravet <1 yr, Lafora 10-18 yr, Rolandic before puberty; seizure types infantile spasms febrile myoclonic CPS atypical absence progressive myoclonic epilepsy SPS infrequent; mental retardation + + - -; other features tuberous sclerosis, AR dementia hallucinations PAS+ve inclusions, m/c seizures in childhood; EEG hypsarrhythmia mountain waves, centrotemporal spikes; histopathology PAS+ intracellular inclusions.
